newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Trans Tasman sees growth from Aust IPO.
newsitem.headline: Trans Tasman sees growth from Aust IPO.

text.p: The public float of Trans Tasman Properties' Australian assets will enable the company to expand its Australian property activities and provide significant enhancements to the value of its listed equity stocks, chairman Sir David Beattie said on Friday.
The Australian assets are to be floated through the listing of Trans Tasman subsidiary Australian Growth Properties, in which Trans Tasman will retain a 41 percent interest.
The public will be offered 180 million A$1 shares and a sub-underwritten 17.5 million shares will be reserved for existing Trans Tasman share and noteholders.
The issue is fully underwritten and will close on April 30.

Beattie said in a statement that the listing provided considerable benefits to Trans Tasman and would enable it to "expand its Australian property activities and in turn provide significant enhancements to the value of the company's listed equity stocks".
He said the consolidated group would receive a NZ$202 million equity infusion from the issue, while debt to total asset ratios would be reduced to under 39 percent from over 50 percent.

Commenting on the retirement of debt made possible by the issue, Beattie said, "On completion of this transaction, Trans Tasman will have eliminated the remaining impediments which the company was burdened with in recent years, and be in a position to move forward as New Zealand's largest listed property company".
Australian Growth Properties will take over a NZ$305 million portfolio, much of it in the Sydney central business district. Its biggest asset is the Landmark Building on George St.
Development approval, granted in December, allows for a 33-storey tower to be added on an adjacent site, on a podium over three heritage buildings.
Trans Tasman Properties is the result of a November 1995 merger between Tasman Properties (the former Robert Jones Investments) and Seabil New Zealand.
